newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mediator hopeful on airline agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mediator hopeful on airline agreement.

text.p: The top U.S. mediator overseeing the dispute between American Airlines and its pilots said on Thursday he was hopeful that an agreement could be worked out that would avert a strike at midnight on Friday.
"I am hopeful, and within the next hour I may be more optimistic," said Kenneth Hipp, chairman of the National Mediation Board.

Hipp, speaking to reporters at a hotel where talks have been taking place, said he anticipated that the two sides in the dispute would meet face-to-face, and that negotiations could go on throughout the night if necessary.
The pilots were expected to present a broad contract proposal to the airline aimed at preventing a strike that would ground the nation's No. 2 carrier.
That proposal was expected to deal with two of the key disputes -- pay for pilots on American's regular flights, and whether union pilots can fly smaller jets for the airline's American Eagle unit.
Hipp declined to give any more details about the status of the negotiations.
